units.translation: in the sense of passing by
Thus Heimsoethius for περῶσα [passing through], which will be discussed under στιβέω [to tread].
But he, not delaying nor heedlessly overcome by sleep, let pass the messenger's part
having let go — I will not speak the penalty
having let pass the roaring of the sea
if you have anything remaining or left aside to tell
but yield the power willingly to me
τὰ παρεστῶτα [the present circumstances] present circumstances
with perfect παρέστηκα [I have stood by] and participle παρεστώς [having stood by], aorist παρέστην [I stood by]
he stands by with a shout
now when it has stood by you
the best of the present circumstances then seemed to me to be
he speaks the best of the present circumstances
we will send forth a Parnassian voice

Thus in this place M, which offers Παρνάσσιος [Parnassian] and Παρνησσίδος [Parnassian] with double sigma at Ch. 952 and 563, which fluctuation is constant in this and similar names ending in σός [with single sigma] or σσός [with double sigma], about which I have spoken in Thes. vol. 6 p. 527. The single sigma is generally in older books: but Eustathius p. 1872, 50 reports that this is of later usage, which also seems to have been the opinion of Herodian, by whom Παρνασσός δύο σσ ἔχον [Parnassus having two sigmas] is placed among oxytones in σός [with single sigma] in Arcadius p. 76, 24 (vol. 1 p. 209, 20 ed. Lentz.)
he came to this land and the seats of Parnassus
and, where the meter demands, πάροιθε [before], a single word, about which see Herodian περὶ μον. λέξ. [on single words] p. 46, 27. It signifies
such a misfortune is at hand for you to lament in addition to the former one
many things having been said before in due season
and who would say that he found gold before me?
and before the prow the sharp spirit of the heart sits
such as the Acheloian maidens of the Strymonian sea are neighbors of the Thracian dwellings
It is constructed with the genitive in the sense of going astray, like ἁμαρτάνειν [to err],

which he said as οἴχομαι φόβῳ [I am gone with fear] at v. 786. The scholiast reads παροίχεται [it has passed by], placing a period after ἐτητύμως [truly], and a comma after εἴ τί μοι [if anything to me]. Hermann restored the correct punctuation. For the particle εἰ [if] is constructed with the words περίφοβόν μ᾿ ἔχει τάρβος [fear holds me exceedingly afraid].
